lead.headline: Supreme Court sets safeguards against misuse of POCSO in custody battles
lead.deck: Where a parent is accused under POCSO during a matrimonial dispute, there is to be no automatic arrest on an FIR, and a child psychiatrist or psychologist must be consulted first.
body: A bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K.V. Viswanathan has laid down safeguards for complaints under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act made against a parent during a matrimonial dispute. Registration of an FIR in such a case will not lead to automatic arrest.

A child psychiatrist or psychologist must be consulted first. On the facts, the Court quashed a mother's FIR against the father, which the CBI had found unsupported, and asked the Family Court to oversee the child's return to him.

POCSO is a strict statute that raises presumptions against the accused so that children are protected quickly. The ruling gives police and courts national guardrails for the narrower situation in which such a complaint is made in the middle of a custody battle.

articles.headline: Only constitutional courts can bar remission, Supreme Court rules
body: In Naval Kishore v. State of Punjab, the Court held that only the Supreme Court and the High Courts can impose a fixed-term or whole-life sentence that excludes remission. A Sessions Court's no-remission life term was replaced with 25 years' rigorous imprisonment without remission.

This 'special category' of sentence was recognised by the Constitution Bench in Union of India v. V. Sriharan (2015). In a separate appeal, a three-judge bench upheld a man's conviction for the rape and murder of his six-year-old stepdaughter but commuted his death sentence to life imprisonment.

cases.name: Waris v. State of Madhya Pradesh

articles.headline: No prior sanction needed before a Magistrate orders an FIR
body: A Magistrate's direction under Section 156(3) CrPC to register an FIR comes before cognizance, the Court held, so sanction under Section 197 to prosecute a public servant is not needed at that stage. The investigation, which the High Court had quashed, will resume.

Section 197 shields public servants from prosecution for acts done in the discharge of official duty unless the government sanctions it, and the bar operates when a court takes cognizance. The ruling separates that bar from the earlier step of setting an investigation in motion.

articles.headline: Custodial confession alone cannot sustain NSA detention
body: A confession made in police custody cannot by itself support a preventive detention order, the Court held. The National Security Act detention of an accused in the Sambhal violence was quashed, and costs of Rs 10 lakh were imposed on Uttar Pradesh.

The ruling protects the Article 22(5) safeguard against detention built on custodial statements. The Bombay High Court likewise set aside an MPDA Act detention, holding that an assumption that the detenu would probably get bail, without material to back it, is not a valid ground.

Aman @ Aman Ibrahim Khan v. The Commissioner of Police, Pune
cases.note: Bombay HC · MPDA detention set aside

articles.headline: Safety audit of Delhi-NCR public spaces ordered within four weeks
body: In the suo motu case on recent rape incidents in Delhi-NCR, the Court directed police to map vulnerable spots district by district, step up patrols and audit street lighting and CCTV, including at transit hubs. Status reports are due in four weeks.

The bench described the incidents as a systemic failure of policing and administration. Separately, the Delhi High Court held that a rape survivor may take part at every stage, including regular bail hearings, and set aside a bail order passed without notice to her.

cases.name: In Re: Recent Rape Incidents in Delhi NCR
Ms G v. State (NCT of Delhi)
cases.note: Delhi HC · survivor to be heard on bail

articles.headline: Rs 1 lakh each for daily-wagers in 25-year-old Bihar dues case
body: Bihar and Jharkhand must pay each daily-wage worker Rs 1 lakh, with 12% interest on delayed provident fund and 6% on delayed wages. The Court rejected a flat Rs 42.50-a-day rate as unfair. Untraced workers get 12 months to claim.

In a separate ruling, the Court held that a senior cannot be paid less than a junior holding the same post. Two lecturers appointed on the same day in 1990 drew different pay after advance increments; the gap had no valid basis and violated the guarantee of equality.

cases.name: Bihar State Ardh Sarkari Arajpati Karamchari Maha Sangh v. State of Bihar
Jai Prakash Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors.

articles.headline: Re-arrest after a vitiated arrest needs a magistrate's reasoned nod
body: Where an accused is freed because the grounds of arrest were not supplied, police need a magistrate's reasoned permission to arrest again, a Delhi High Court Division Bench held. Re-arresting the accused merely because charges had been added was illegal.

The ruling lays down the procedure to follow after a breach of Article 22(1), which requires that an arrested person be informed of the grounds of arrest as soon as may be. Without that step, a fresh arrest cannot cure the earlier illegality.

cases.name: Manoj Chaudhary v. State (NCT of Delhi)

articles.headline: Plastic warnings stay; Centre may use patent law for costly drugs
body: The Madras High Court rejected FSSAI's review of its order requiring warnings about micro- and nano-plastics on packs of water, salt and sugar, holding that consumers have a right to know.

The Kerala High Court held that Section 100 of the Patents Act lets the Centre make and supply patented medicines for non-commercial government use, and said this is warranted where life-saving drugs are priced out of reach.

cases.name: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India v. G. Subramania Koushik
In Re Exorbitant Pricing of Life Saving Patented Medicines

articles.headline: Bar Council told to frame a minimum stipend for junior advocates
body: The Madhya Pradesh High Court directed the State Bar Council to frame guidelines on a minimum stipend for junior advocates within six months. It suggested Rs 20,000 a month in cities and Rs 15,000 in rural areas, for three years.
In Delhi, the High Court imposed costs of Rs 1 lakh on counsel who joined a virtual hearing from a moving car, holding that this breached the video-conferencing rules.

policy.headline: Collegium recommends three High Court Chief Justices for the Supreme Court
policy.text: Chief Justices Sunita Agarwal (Gujarat), Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya (Delhi) and Aparesh Kumar Singh (Telangana) were recommended on 28 September. The names now go to the Centre for notification.

policy.headline: RBI cuts export-realisation deadline from 15 months to 9
policy.text: Amended FEMA export-import regulations require exporters to realise and repatriate proceeds within 9 months, or 12 months for rupee-invoiced exports. The changes take effect on 1 October 2026.

policy.headline: Pension cover extended to EPF members earning up to ₹25,000 a month
policy.text: A Labour Ministry notification of 25 September amends the Employees' Pension Scheme, 2026 with effect from 17 September. Members at or below the new wage ceiling may join even if earlier left out.

policy.headline: FSSAI to adopt red-hexagon warnings for foods high in sugar, fat or salt
policy.text: FSSAI told the Supreme Court it will follow Canada's front-of-pack model. Draft regulations are planned in about four months, with a 60-day consultation and a 365-day voluntary window.
